messages:
marie: FYI — sales handed two enterprise asks that touch SLA, uptime, and latency guarantees. need a quick intake and routing plan so we can get scoping + pricing.
alex: quick summary? which customers and what SLAs are they asking for?
marie: Customer A (FintechCo) wants 99.99% uptime for hosted inference + P50 <= 50ms for text-generation API at our current commit level. Customer B (MediCo) needs 99.995% uptime in a VPC/private deploy + 99.9% support SLA (24/7 on-call) and data residency.
sam: sounds like FintechCo could be solved with Dedicated + routing policy + higher priority support. MediCo likely Private/on-prem and SOC/compliance review.
jordan: agree. do we have any capacity or perf numbers for sustained P50=50ms at production load? infra-bot: perf-matrix: note — current hosted median P50 for gpt-lite-8b is 65ms at 1k qps; 50ms achieved only with batching tweaks and quantization on specific HW.
alex: ok so we need two asks: 1) SLA exception intake doc that lists customer, requested SLOs, required configuration, and allowed fallbacks; 2) routing + escalation playbook (who owns ops, who gets paged at what time bands).
marie: i drafted a minimal intake checklist we can use for sales->product handoff. dropping it here for feedback:
```
- customer: name + primary contact
- deployment preference: hosted / dedicated / private
- requested uptime SLO (e.g., 99.99)
- latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99) and endpoints affected
- expected qps / concurrency profile
- data residency / compliance needs
- support tier needed (business / enterprise / 24/7)
- acceptable fallbacks (lower perf model, cross-region failover)
- financial terms / commitment (reserved capacity?)
- launch readiness date
```
alicia: the checklist looks good. suggest adding "regression eval set + perf test window" so research can validate quality after quantization.
sam: +1. also include "rollback trigger thresholds" for latency and error rates.
jordan: who is going to be the routing owner? product triage or sales ops? i think product should own initial triage, then hand to eng-infra for cost/perf feasibility and to security for compliance.
marie: proposal: product owns intake and initial priority (P0/P1), sales ops owns contract negotiation, eng-infra owns perf/capacity assessment, eng-security owns compliance signoff, support/onsite owns escalation + 24/7 staffing. if Dedicated/Private is needed, sales ops and finance must surface commit terms.
alex: agree. let's add a small escalation matrix to the playbook. draft below:
```
- P0 (outage or severe SLA gap): page oncall infra + eng-sre + product owner -> 15m response
- P1 (degradation affecting customer SLO): open ticket, notify sales ops & customer success -> 1 hour response
- P2 (new request scoping/contract work): product + sales ops sync -> 3 business days
```
marie: good. next steps:
- product: finalize intake template and add to Confluence (owner: marie) — due EOD Tue
- eng-infra: run perf feasibility for FintechCo target (owner: jordan) — initial results Wed
- eng-security: list compliance gating items for MediCo (owner: alicia) — first pass Thu
- sales ops: confirm commitment window & finance model (owner: lucas in sales ops) — Wed
sam: i'll also add an item for Optimize team to run batching/quantization experiments and share cost delta.
alex: do we need an immediate communication to the customers about expected timeline? sales should send a quick "we're evaluating feasibility" note to set expectations.
marie: yup. i'll ping sales to send a 48h ack and include the intake checklist as part of the ask.
infra-bot: note — placing a capacity hold request requires ticket to eng-infra with expected qps and target SLOs. template: `POST /capacity-requests {customer, qps, model, slox}`
alicia: tagging eng-security for MediCo: @alicia @eng-security please review data residency constraints once we have the customer requirements.
marie: thanks everyone. i'll drop the intake doc into #product-resources and link the confluence page here once it's up. :thumbsup:
